title: Xfce 4.22 Working Toward Early 2027 Release
byline: Written by Michael Larabel in Desktop on 17 November 2026 at 05:50 AM EST. 17 Comments
excerpt: Next month marks two years since the Xfce 4.20 release
content_html:
Next month marks two years since the Xfce 4.20 release. Its successor, Xfce 4.22, looks like it will be out in early 2027.

The Xfce 4.22 roadmap was updated on the Xfce desktop project's Wiki this week. An Xfce 4.22pre1 release is now scheduled to happen on 15 December that also marks the feature freeze and string freeze.

One month later on 15 January, the Xfce 4.22pre2 release is expected that will also mark the code freeze for Xfce 4.22.

Yet to be finalized is the Xfce 4.22pre3 milestone and the final freeze. After that is then the final Xfce 4.22 release on a date to be determined. Typically though between the different pre-release milestones and official Xfce release is just a matter of weeks. Long story short, the stable release of the Xfce 4.22 desktop will more than likely be out sometime in Q1'2027.

The Xfce 4.22 roadmap can be found on the Xfce Wiki.

Xfce 4.22 is bringing more work on their Wayland support, panel and core improvements, better HiDPI handling, and other changes. The ongoing Wayland enablement remains a big focus and the current Wayland details for Xfce can be found via this roadmap page.
